A commenter was confused by the claim of "SHA256 encryption to ensure your user's data will always be safe" and pointed out that SHA256 is a hash function, not an encryption method.
Security concern: from the docs, Belvo appears to send security key passwords over email, apparently only by email. The commenter called this "shaky at best."
Positive: a commenter liked that the docs include a ready-made Postman collection.
Criticism: the homepage looked like a "nearly autogenerated landing page for the docs site" and "doesn't inspire confidence." The commenter urged the team to invest in a new homepage.
QOL request: on the institutions page of the developer docs, add links to the sites of the listed banks.
A commenter called it "a big no-no" that Belvo connects through bank websites and requires end users to hand over their website banking credentials.
Praise: "Your API looks very clean."
Docs UX issue: clicking "Run" next to each script snippet takes 2-3 seconds, with no loading animation to show anything is happening. The commenter suggested adding a loading indicator.

Sign-up bug: after the first page, the second step showed a generic "retry later" error, and clicking again did nothing. Dev tools revealed "This user is already signed up," and the account turned out to be created. The user asked for clearer error messages, especially for a finance product.

An open banking developer compared Belvo to TrueLayer for Latin America. They asked where the user authentication flow is and noted that, even in the UK, few people are willing to log into their bank via a third-party app. Trust can't be built with technology alone.
